title: A demo client for mimid, in ParlorVTC's shape
description:
Mark 2026-11-23: "we might have to write somethign like Parler jsut for
mimid demo".

WHY IT IS NEEDED. mimid ships no UI (decision mimid-1wgh.38) and no
stock JMAP Chat client implements draft-atwood-jmap-vtc, so nothing can
show the call work: the room, the signalling, the keying and the JMAP
surface are all built and no human can see them.

THE SHAPE TO COPY, from MarkAtwood/ParlorVTC: two HTML files with inline
CSS and JS, ~1100 lines of ES modules, no build step, no dependencies,
no npm, runs from file://. Separate repo, so decision mimid-1wgh.38
stands: mimid still ships no UI.

WHAT IT DOES, in order:
1. authenticates to the agent's loopback endpoint with the local token
   or an app password (docs/design/frontend-auth.md §3);
2. reads the Session's urn:ietf:params:jmap:vtc capability for
   iceServers and supportsMimiCalls (commit c46f9dba);
3. starts a call with VTCCall/set create, callType "room" and the
   chatId of the chat to call;
4. sends offer, answer and candidates with VTCCall/signal;
5. RECEIVES them -- which is bead mimid-1wgh.114.8 and does not exist
   yet. BLOCKED on that;
6. does the media with WebRTC, lifting Parlor's web/webrtc.js nearly
   unchanged: the ICE servers from step 2, Opus constrained to 24kbps
   mono, an explicit audio transceiver so renegotiation works.

THE SHORTEST DEMO NEEDS NO MEDIA SECRET. A 1:1 WebRTC call is
DTLS-SRTP, already end to end encrypted, and the session descriptions
carrying those fingerprints are authenticated by MLS, so no fingerprint
comparison is needed either (bead mimid-1wgh.114.5). SFrame, an SFU and
VTCCall/exportMediaSecret are what the GROUP case needs. Do the 1:1
first: it is the demo, and it is reachable.

WHAT TO TAKE FROM PARLOR BESIDES THE WEBRTC, each of which it learned
the hard way and commented:
- buffer candidates until the remote description is set, both sides
  (pendingIce), because arrival order is not processing order;
- an idempotency guard on the offer ("if (state.pc) return");
- a bounded seen-ids set with signature-verify-before-insert, so a
  duplicate cannot poison the cache;
- validate every field's type before using it.
mimid does not need Parlor's sender check (ev.pubkey comparison "to
prevent injection attacks"): participantId is server-set from the
authenticated MLS sender, which is the one place this design is
stronger than Parlor's.
notes:
DISCUSSED WITH MARK 2026-11-23. This bead described the BUILD well and
understated the OBSTACLES. Four corrections, and a split that matters.

1. THE HTML IS THE EASY PART; THE SETUP IS THE COST.

ParlorVTC needs nothing: open a file, share a link. Its signalling is
public relays and its identity an ephemeral key, so there is no server
and no account. mimid's demo needs, before anyone speaks: a provider
running; two agents, each with its own store and credential; two
accounts on that provider; consent between those two users; a chat
between them; and then two browser tabs each pasting a credential.

That is the barrier to "fast and easy demo", not the ~1100 lines of
JavaScript. Any estimate of this bead that counts only the client is
wrong.

2. SPLIT IT: A RUST TEST FOR THE PROTOCOL, HTML FOR THE MEDIA.

Steps 1 to 5 above -- the Session, VTCCall/set, VTCCall/signal, and
receiving VTCCallSignal -- are HTTP and WebSocket and nothing else. No
browser is needed for any of it. mimid's own suite can drive the whole
protocol half headlessly against two in-process agents, exactly as
mimid-agent-jmap tests/two_accounts.rs already does for chat. Only step
6, the media, needs a browser.

WHY THIS IS THE IMPORTANT PART, with today's evidence: the candidate
signal was being sent with NO PAYLOAD AT ALL (vtc_stream.rs put None in
sdp and null in candidate). It compiled, it linted, and every test
passed. A human would have found it by making a call and hearing
silence, and would have had no idea which of six layers was wrong. A
protocol test asserting "the candidate that arrives equals the candidate
that was sent" catches that in CI, forever. The bug was found by clippy
by luck, not by design.

So the deliverables are two, and the test is the one that keeps the
feature honest:
- a Rust integration test, in mimid, driving two agents through a whole
  call negotiation over the JMAP surface;
- the HTML page, in its own repo, for the media and for showing people.

3. ONE FILE, NOT TWO. Parlor is two files because it is ASYMMETRIC: a
host who admits, a visitor who queues, different screens. A mimid call
is symmetric -- both sides are MLS members with agents and the same
rights -- so there is one page, and whoever clicks first is the offerer.

4. THE CREDENTIAL IS AN APP PASSWORD, NOT THE LOCAL TOKEN. The local
token is the admin credential, in a 0600 file, and derives the
attachment-link key (decision mimid-1wgh.88); handing it to a browser
page is the wrong grant. The credential table already holds app
passwords as SCRAM-SHA-256 verifiers (docs/design/frontend-auth.md §3),
which is what a page should be given.

5. CORS: A file:// PAGE SENDS "Origin: null". Checked the agent's
handling: allowed_origin matches the Origin header against
allowed_origins by exact string, so allowed_origins = ["null"] works
for a page opened from the filesystem. It is ugly, and the alternative
is serving the page from somewhere with a real origin. DECIDE WHICH,
because "open this HTML file" and "run a web server first" are
different promises to whoever is being shown the demo.

STILL BLOCKED ON NOTHING NOW: bead mimid-1wgh.114.8's WebSocket is
written (the signal stream and the socket), so step 5 exists. The
protocol test can be written immediately and does not need the page.
